# READ ME FIRST


**NOTE ABOUT SOUND LEVELS (LUFS)**:

- "Normalising" will raise (or reduce) the inbound audio level based on the loudest moment in all of it. This makes it the best level control at this stage without effecting the sound (compression, eq, expanding, reverb, and all that stuff, leave all that to post production imo).

- I set ambient levels to about -40 LUFs, dialogue audio to -23 or -16 LUFS, depending on level I want. For a guide, Spotify forces all audio to -14 LUFS, but you want to leave some headroom for post-production and to be sure to avoid clipping, so I dont go above -16 LUFS and lean into -23 more often.  

**ISSUES WITH LIPSYNC WHEN DRIVEN BY AUDIO OF DIALOGUE THAT HAS A LOT OF SILENT MOMENTS**:

- LTX 2.3 I find using audio in often doesnt work for lipsync and the mouth wont move if there isnt a lot of audio dialogue. The trick is to add ambient audio in to the full length just room or environment sound (see the audio merge node, adjust LUFS to get levels, use "mean" to blend the two audio files - dialogue and ambient, but watch out for clipping, also you dont want the ambient audio driving action, just enough volume to not be dead silence). 

- This wasnt needed in LTX 2. but is needed in LTX 2.3. I downloaded 10 seconds of room ambience from freesound.org. You dont have to add it to the resulting video and it doesnt have to be audible, just something that is getting rid of the absolute silence should work. If you have a lot of dialogue then it usually isnt needed. - Mark, May 2026.

- put longest audio in "audio1" slot of audio merge
- confirm the correct audio selection is connected to the next stage node.
- confirm you have connected this audio to the LTXVConcatAVLatent node.
- Connect the audio output option you want saved to the video combine node in the final output.

If you get weird NaN errors with FFMPEG confirm the preview is the correct length, and confirm both audio files inbound are the same, recommend using 32 bit float, 44.1khz, mp3 for both if you are uncertain. You can use Audacity (free open source software) to check and change formats.

using prompt relay is necessary if it was used in the i2v structure stage when creating the initial video. I find disabling all loras other than the distill is needed, else it can cause issues with multi-characters (possibly due to loras not being trained on more than 2 characters generally).

switching between prompt relay and the usual text prompt should only require reconnecting the positive and negative colour reroutes below. then disable or enable the relevant prompt node.

more info on using prompt relay is in the i2v workflow.

# INBOUND VIDEO RESIZING

in: 480 x 277 (16:9) (LTX reduces it: 480 x 256)
in: 480 x 201 (2.39:1) (LTX reduces it: 480 x 192)

doesnt matter what size video is coming in, reduce it to 480 on the longer edge else it will not come out at 1920 on the longer edge after upscaling.

# TEMPORAL UPSCALING GROUP

Keep this bypassed unless you need to address motion issues (it adds 1/3rd of time to my runs).

It works by doubling your set fps (targeting 50fps is known for fixing motion issues) going into the 2nd upscale sampler. This will also downscale back to your original fps by using a "every 2nd frame" output save that is connected after the vae decoder (but stored in the group so you can bypass it too).

on my rig this turned a 14 min wf into a 22 min wf and introduces distillated artefacts but does fix motion. bypass this group if you dont need it or experiment.

NOTES: I originally plugged this in after the upscale and inbound ref images nodes, but it changed the people (structure was same) so putting it at first stage before the 2nd upscaler to see how it goes.

You may need ref images set to 1 strength as the temporal upscaler seems to change things (removed mans glasses that were in FF str set to 0.7).

# 1ST SAMPLER SAVE OUTPUT GROUP

When seed hunting and testing I enable this group to confirm results leaving the 1st sampler. Its most useful when complex prompt relay steps are involved to know where in the process the results might be failing (and where they are working).

# AUDIO OUT CONNECTORS

choose from 3 options or disconnect if you dont want audio saved out. See the notes with other audio connectors colored similarly. (color does not necessarily match its just to make it easier to see in the wf)

# AUDIO-IN GROUP

This could probably be tidied up a bit but I am still experimenting with dialogue setups - Mark , May 2026.

- I set "window_size_seconds" node to 20 for 20 seconds, or 10 for 10 seconds. In this workflow the video inbound controls the length of the frames - Mark, May 2026.

The connectors for audio are whether you need the audio merge node feature to blend in with your dialogue audio, or just the dialogue. Ambient sound is used to overcome the issue with mouth movement failing when only short dialogue audio is used and long silences occur, which in LTX 2.3 can cause lipsync failure (see other notes in group for details). 

I recommend using Audacity free software to make your audio exactly how you want it, blend -40 LUFS level ambience in with your dialogue set to -23LUFS. and use that as mp3 at 44.1Khz sampling rate. Then you have easy control of audio and when it happens.

I talk about that in this video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNqiqEzTKD8

# VAE DECODE NODE

Tiled used to be necessary and that has changed.

Kijai fixed up the VAE decode to work better and use less memory sometime in April and since then I have not experienced an OOM. This is partly also thanks to ComfyUI's dynamic VRAM. If you have up to date comfyui then I recommend using the VAE decode not the tiled one. 

There is also a Patch Triton VAE if you can make use of it. as of June 2026. I get "pin errors" but it works and speeds it up a bit.

# TEST NOTES FOR PROMPT RELAY AND MANAGING MOUTH CLONING ISSUES

I am trying to solve the "mouth cloning" issue between same genders, and looking for patterns to target.

## SOLUTIONS:

-  **If getting mouth cloning only in the final 2nd sampler upscale stage**. Lower sigmas to 0.73, 0.55, 0.29, 0.0 for last sampler stage, alternatively try lcm as that worked even at higher sigmas, but it did have slight eye failure but barely noticable.

## PATTERNS OBSERVED

- if the same gender is stood next to a targetted dialogue person they will mouth clone.

- using Prompt Relay segment example, `The black woman on the right says in a dejected tone, "god damn it"` . This will work most of the time and the woman next to her will not mouth clone until the final upscaler stage if I get the seed right. but using `The black woman in the leopard print dress on the right says in a dejected tone, "god damn it"` causes the woman next to her to mouth clone. I have seen this a few times now, suggesting only one single targetted adjective description is useful and multiple adjectives can cause failure but positional are also useful, I am not sure hair or dressage always is.

- the main culprit for mouth cloning is the final 2nd sampler stage going from 960 long edge to 1920 and I am not yet sure why. Even though only 4 steps and starting at 0.09, it is adding in mouth cloning to the same-gender neighbour of any people with dialogue. Even going from i2v stage into the 1st Sampler (saved out to video, also to latent for testing) it works fine, just the last stage adds mouth cloning back in.

Static camera shows a man on the left with medium length hair in jacket, a brunette woman in black pants and a leather vest, a blonde woman in a blue dress in the middle, and a black woman on the right in a leopard print dress, waiting inside an elevator. everyone stays in frame the entire time. camera remains static.

The black woman on the right turns and says dismissively, "Well I’m not fucking him in the lift, that’s for sure." and shakes her head | The blonde woman says, "Don’t matter, we are still on the clock. So pay up mister, you can have a little play with my titties once I see some cash." | The brunette woman remains silent

I think of this sigma stuff like "Dynamic Denoise". 

default to 0.97.

set the start_value to 1 and it  will drive it with the prompt and ref images more fully, which can lead to changes in behaviour from the original video.

set it to less (0.98 to 0.99, you dont have to go too low) and it will honour the original video more.

LTX 2.3 LORAS:

the distill lora can use 384 but it is 7GB and the Kijai (see his hugging face) one listed is only 2.5GB but about as good. setting seems to be 0.4 to 0.6. Keep checking his HF repo for the latest.

I am now using VBVR set around 0.4 to 1.0 which is a reasoning lora and seems to help with v2v physics and adherance to the video in most cases - https://huggingface.co/LiconStudio/Ltx2.3-VBVR-lora-I2V/tree/main

Testing

- OmniNFT is the Kijai version (readme notes on it say use strength 2.0) https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/blob/main/loras/README.md

# REF IMAGES

I only do FF or FF + LF here (First Frame/Last frame).
(I dont use Kijai nodes for middle frames I have another workflow for that.)

index_2 set to -1 means last image.

two nodes are required here; one for each upscaling stage.

"With straight i2v I usually turn the imgtovidinplace strength down to 0.8 and that helps I think official has 0.7 on first then 1 on second. I prefer the 0.8 on both." - anon.

# CHANGES AS OF 29th JUNE 2026

- Added RTX NVIDIA upscaler takes final output to 4K. Disable if you dont want it. 

- Changed 1st Sampler to 12 steps

- Changed 2nd Sampler sigmas increased by 1 set and changed to new numbers (testing). Also changed from Euler_Ancestral to LCM on 2nd Sampler (its faster and I feel smoother which I prefer, you can select your preference).

- Change img ref inbound strength for First Frame to 0.7 and Last Frame to 1.0 as standard - been reading a lot of reasons why less than 1.0 on first frame is better.

- For NSFW or "mature theme art work" download and use the "heretic abliterated" Lora from Kijai on hugging face instead of changing the text encoder is recommended best practise.



# NEW THINGS OF 16th JUNE 2026

two slight speed ups added to workflow

1. **patch triton vae** is from Kiaji and improves memory with VAE you can disable if you are not keeping comfyui and his nodes up to date. *(disabled it for now as I get pin errors and no speed up value, others may find it useful.)* </br>

2. **Test fp8 model to replace the LTX 2.3 Q5KM GGUF** as with ComfyUI changes the dynamic memory is now so good it might be faster. *(LLMs said: "For your RTX 3060 12GB, the best balance of speed and visual quality is the LTX 2.3 dev model used alongside the Distilled LoRA (or a Q8/Q6 GGUF version of the dev model). This setup fits entirely into your VRAM") NOTE: Because its using a raw transformer model all-in-one checkpoint, you must separate the model into individual components (this workflow does that already) </br>
   - (The fp8 model currently requires adding some of the switches back in to the bat file run else it wont work on my 3060 RTX. fastest was with only --lowvram added back in.)*
</br>
subtitles, text, blurry, low quality, watermark, overlay, titles, scene change, flashing lights,

chunk may not be needed if dynamic vram working and it all fits in, else use it but dont do more than 2 is recommendation - March 2026.

If using dynamic vram apparently "Model Memory Usage Factor Overwride
" node also is not used, according to Kijai. (But I leave it enabled because I have to add disable switches in to bat file when using batch runs).

# 3 OPTIONS FOR AUDIO

choose your connector and plug it into the "audio_latent" slot of the 1st upscaler groups "LTXVConcatAVLatent" node. You dont need to bypass the others, just switch out the connector, but it might be best to bypass in some situations. also check which audio is being saved to the final Video Combine node.

1. "Empty Latent Audio" (A) (use this as default so it doesnt error)
use this if you are prompting dialogue or dont care about audio.

2. Use "Audio From Video Group" (B)
Use this if you want to keep the audio from the video all the way through and drive lipsync from it too.

3. Use "Audio-In Group" (C) if you want to drive the lipsync and dialogue from an audio file.
